results.title: Top Emerging Life Sciences Trends to Watch in 2026
results.content: I keep noticing the same handful of forces converging in biotech and pharma – AI advancing as an operational partner, advanced manufacturing, and the concurring evolution of the regulatory framework. One of the most exciting medical device industry trends is how generative AI is transforming device design. Regulatory bodies explicitly expect AI-driven MedTech to embed robust quality, safety, and transparency controls into their devices, as became evident when the Medical Device Coordination Group (MDCG) published the guidance document MDCG 2025-6: FAQ on Interplay between the Medical Devices Regulation & In vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices Regulation and the Artificial Intelligence Act in June 2025. Some emerging trends in life sciences aren’t confined to just biotech, pharma, or MedTech - they traverse industries and shape the life sciences landscape as a whole. Partnering with Scilife can help teams and organizations translate these emerging trends in life sciences into practical strategies, navigate regulatory complexity, and turn the challenges of 2026 into opportunities for growth.

results.title: Recent progress in CRISPR-based microfluidic assays and applications
results.content: In this review, we illustrate the recent progress as well as our work and collaborative work in CRISPR-based microfluidic detection assays based on the categories of microfluidic chips, including paper-based microfluidics, centrifugal microfluidics, digital microfluidics, electrochemical microfluidics and wearable microfluidics, mainly focusing on how microfluidic platforms improve CRISPR-based detection method in the aspect of visualization, detection throughput, anti-contamination, simple operation, sensitivity, specificity and quantification, etc. Microfluidic detection methods seem to continue to be rapid progress in the future and microfluidic platforms have the potential to take CRISPR-based technologies to the new level in the field of bioanalysis and clinical diagnosis. results.title: Medical Device Validation in 2025 | Kneat
results.content: * Medical device validation in 2025. # Medical device validation in 2025. Validation teams in the medical device sector are under more pressure than ever. Our new whitepaper, ***Validation Strategies in Medical Devices*** , has the answers. ## Validation challenges in the med device industry. Validation in the medical device sector is uniquely complex. Add to this the constantly evolving **EU MDR requirements**, multi-phase product lifecycles, and the need for continuous re-validation after even minor design or supplier changes, and it’s clear why validation remains a persistent challenge. **Want to dive deeper?** Read our Medical Devices eBook ***Simplifying and Streamlining Medical Device Validation*** to explore the biggest validation challenges facing the industry — and how digital solutions are helping teams overcome them. According to the **2025 State of Validation study**, which surveyed **300+ validation professionals worldwide**, including a focused group of **96 respondents from the med device sector**, teams are juggling more complexity, higher workloads, and growing compliance demands. Nearly **70% of medical device professionals report increasing validation workloads** in 2025, but more than half of teams still have six or fewer members. Digital validation adoption is accelerating. Half of med device organizations have **fully adopted or are actively implementing digital validation systems** and early adopters are seeing strong ROI.
